rendered: The review starts from the known global cobalt reserves, given as 7 million metric tons[1], taken from the United States Geological Survey report on cobalt. It then applies a conservative mining efficiency of ≈70%[2] per year, and assumes that ≈40%[3] of the mined cobalt is directed toward battery manufacturing. Applying the efficiency and the battery share to the reserves, the review states that the total usable battery-specific cobalt from the total reserves comes to ≈2 million[4] of cobalt, which is the amount it reports.[5]
